clue.text: Abraham consumes roots, being an Australian

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so the short form of Abraham swallows the other piece

parts.note: Abe is the familiar short form of Abraham
your roots are your origin

explanation.surface: Someone called Abraham eats roots, which is taken as proof he is Australian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roots' looks botanical, but it means where you come from. 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aborigine is one of the original native peoples of the continent, so an Australian by birth.

clue.text: Since embracing a girl, remains!

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold around, so the word for since wraps the girl

parts.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it was raining'
she is a pronoun standing for a girl

explanation.surface: An exclamation that ever since someone hugged a girl, she has stayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes are what is left after cremation or burning, a person's mortal remains.

clue.text: Convenient harbour a Parisian used after work

indicators.note: after places the harbour-and-French pieces behind the word for work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
a port is a harbour
une is French for a, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A handy harbour that a Parisian used after a day's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is a link; the order is OP, then PORT, then UNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opportune comes at a suitable, well-timed moment, so it is handy.

clue.text: One new to false teeth contracts

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
dentures are sets of false teeth

explanation.surface: Someone getting used to false teeth for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. 'contracts' looks like a verb (shrinks) but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Indentures are formal agreements, especially binding an apprentice to a master.

clue.text: Pity Len works clumsily

indicators.note: works here means is worked over or kneaded, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A man called Len is to be pitied for doing his job badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' rearranges the letters of PITY LEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something ineptly means doing it without skill, awkwardly.

clue.text: Mathematical problems are upsetting Dutch scholar

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting means turning upside down, so the run is read from the bottom

parts.note: sums are arithmetic problems
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Dutch academic is upset by tricky maths problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns SUMS ARE to give ERA SMUS, reading upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was the great Renaissance humanist from the Netherlands.

clue.text: Curse Sunday clothes

parts.note: wear means clothing, as in evening wear

explanation.surface: Grumbling about having to put on one's Sunday best.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to use bad language, to utter oaths.

clue.text: Hospital broadcast is about entertainment

indicators.note: is about means goes around, so the word for broadcast wraps the letter

parts.note: to sow seed is to broadcast it, scattering it widely
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital radio broadcast is all about entertaining patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' is the farming sense, scattering seed: SOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A show is a performance put on for an audience.

clue.text: Dread having lost time slip

indicators.note: losing a letter means taking it away from the word for dread

parts.note: terror is extreme dread

explanation.surface: Someone afraid of slipping up once they have run out of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake, a blunder.

clue.text: Fragrance noticed once elder is replanted

indicators.note: replanting moves things to new positions, as the letters are moved here

explanation.surface: A gardener notices a scent once the elder bush is moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is replanted' rearranges ONCE ELDER. 'noticed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolence is a pleasant smell, a sweet scent.

clue.text: Trusted to chop edible part only

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A cook was trusted to chop just the edible bits.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'cHOP EDible'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have hoped is to have trusted that something would happen.

clue.text: Delighted our Editor after getting name wrong

indicators.note: after places OUR and the editor's abbreviation behind the scrambled name
getting a word wrong means scrambling its letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Our editor was pleased, having got someone's name wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges NAME to ENAM; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enamoured is being charmed or captivated, thoroughly pleased with something.

clue.text: Season well with thyme, say

parts.note: a spring is a natural well, water rising from the ground

indicators.note: say signals that the herb's name is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: the herb thyme is pronounced like time

explanation.surface: Cooking advice: season the dish well with thyme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' looks like a cooking verb but is the noun, a time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Springtime is the season between winter and summer.

clue.text: Said to be just not married

indicators.note: not married means without the letter for married, so it is removed

parts.note: just means righteous or moral

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that a couple are merely not married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken rather than written.

clue.text: Impound cafe in cost exercise

indicators.note: exercise means working something over, so the letters are put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: A cafe faces seizure as part of a cost-cutting drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercise' rearranges CAFE IN COST.
explanation.definitionFit: To confiscate is to seize property by authority.

clue.text: Upper-class game a guy arranged here

parts.note: U is the British label for upper-class usage
RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An upper-class person sets up a game for a chap somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns A GUY into GUAY. 'here' points at the country the wordplay builds.
explanation.definitionFit: The wordplay names a place, and 'here' stands for that South American country.

clue.text: Natural fuel keepers of the peace rushed round

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, runs peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for rushed goes around the fuel

parts.note: sped means rushed
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers hurried to bring fuel to a region.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unspoiled is untouched, in its original state.

clue.text: South-East and North winds cut

indicators.note: winds here is the verb, twisting the letters into another order

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: The south-east and north winds are dying down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' looks like a noun about weather but rearranges SE and NORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten something is to make it less long, to trim it.

clue.text: Strain leg moving figures

indicators.note: moving means the letters shift into new places

explanation.surface: An athlete straining a leg while running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges STRAIN LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Triangles are three-sided geometric shapes.

clue.text: Female worker bearing illicit alcohol

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
a worker bee is the classic crossword worker
N, north, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A woman at work is carrying contraband booze.
explanation.walkthrough: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking den, especially in Ireland and South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The word for an illegal drinking house stands here for the illicit liquor sold there.

clue.text: Turned on crazy crossword compiler caught wandering!

indicators.note: turned means turned back, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: mad means crazy
the setter refers to themselves as I
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A crazed setter is spotted roaming about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' reverses ON to NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic means roving from place to place with no fixed home.

clue.text: American-backed office lacking nothing to do

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the abbreviation is reversed
lacking means without, so a letter is taken out of the word office

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An office funded by America has nothing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses US to SU; 'lacking' removes O from OFFICE to leave FFICE.
explanation.definitionFit: If something will suffice, it will do, it is enough.

clue.text: Pity to make a hole in solid fat

indicators.note: in places the word for making a hole inside the word for pity

parts.note: sin, as in 'it's a sin', means a pity
to tear something is to make a hole in it

explanation.surface: A shame to rip a hole in a lump of hard fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stearin is the solid component of animal fats used in candles.

clue.text: Resistance units circle vessel

parts.note: O is shaped like a circle
HMS, His or Her Majesty's Ship, prefixes a British naval vessel

explanation.surface: A ship sailing in a circle is resisting.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical resistance is measured in units named after Georg Ohm.

clue.text: Guide to leave without greeting timber supplier

parts.note: a map is a guide to an area

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the greeting is taken out

parts.note: ave is the Latin greeting, hail

explanation.surface: A guide leaves without saying hello to the timber merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes AVE out of LEAVE to leave LE.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a tree, and trees supply wood.

clue.text: Cold individual into mail distribution

indicators.note: into places the individual inside the rearranged mail
distribution means sharing out, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: a person is an individual

explanation.surface: Someone joins the post room to help sort the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' reads as an illness or the weather, but here it describes a manner lacking warmth. 'distribution' gives IMAL, which opens to hold the person.
explanation.definitionFit: Impersonal means lacking warmth or human feeling, so it is cold.

clue.text: Garden plot usually includes this flower

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so the run of letters is inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A garden plot generally has this bloom in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'pLOT USually'; 'this' is a link pointing to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water plant with large showy blooms.

clue.text: US state motorway is quiet

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
M is the British abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: An American state's freeway is peaceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm means still, tranquil and without noise.

clue.text: Part Scandinavian cat?

explanation.surface: A cat that is partly Scandinavian.
explanation.walkthrough: Lapland is part of Scandinavia; a cat that jumps on your knees lands on your lap.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Lapland comes from part of Scandinavia, and a pet that settles on a lap is a lap-dweller.

clue.text: Distribute fifty in a great deal

indicators.note: in places the Roman numeral inside the phrase for a lot

parts.note: a lot means a great deal
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Sharing out fifty in one big transaction.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to give out shares, to apportion.

clue.text: Imagine seeing Doctor East before dinner!

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, is before noon, when dinner was traditionally the midday meal

explanation.surface: A doctor from the east turning up ahead of the evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing' is a link. In older or regional British use dinner is the midday meal, so the morning comes before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream is to picture something in the mind, to fancy it.

clue.text: Count on point being accepted by widespread agreement

indicators.note: being accepted by means taken in, so the word for count holds the other pieces

parts.note: a census is an official count of the population
taken as written
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A nobleman relying on a point that wins broad support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman but is a census.
explanation.definitionFit: Consensus is general accord reached by most of a group.
